assumptions.assumption: the fault queue is left at 1 (CONFIG[1:0] = 00).
assumptions.reason: the request does not ask for filtering of the alarm.

assumptions.assumption: T_HYST stays at its power-on value (5 C).

behaviour: I2C waveforms as an open-drain master with Q = QUARTER clocks - START SDA low, wait 2Q, SCL low, wait Q; each of the 9 bits of a byte - set SDA, wait Q, release SCL and wait until it is seen high (stretching), wait 2Q, sample, SCL low, wait Q; repeated START - release SDA, wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, SDA low, wait 2Q, SCL low, wait Q; STOP - SDA low, wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, release SDA, wait 2Q.
The lines are only pulled low or released.

A write to CTRL with bit 0 = 1 while BUSY = 0 configures - TEMP, MAX, MIN, SAMPLES and VALID are cleared, NACK cleared, then three write transactions to address 0x4B in this order - [START, 0x96, 0x03, 0x90, STOP] (CONFIG - 16-bit resolution, comparator mode, INT active low, fault queue 1); [START, 0x96, 0x04, THIGH[15:8], THIGH[7:0], STOP]; [START, 0x96, 0x06, TLOW[15:8], TLOW[7:0], STOP].
After the third transaction CONFIGURED is set (even if a NACK occurred) and polling begins. Writes to CTRL while BUSY are ignored; a later configure repeats the sequence and restarts the statistics.

While CONFIGURED, a reading starts PERIOD_CYCLES clocks after the previous one started (the first PERIOD_CYCLES clocks after the configure sequence ends) - [START, 0x96, 0x00, repeated START, 0x97, read MSB with ACK, read LSB with NACK, STOP]. Never a STOP between the pointer write and the read (the sensor would lose its pointer).
A reading with no NACK sets TEMP = {MSB, LSB}, SAMPLES += 1, and MAX / MIN (compared as signed 16-bit) - the first reading after a configure sets both; VALID is set.
If any byte of a transaction is NACKed, the master sends STOP after that byte, NACK is set (sticky until the next configure), and a reading is discarded.
BUSY is 1 during the configure sequence and during each reading.
ALARM = NOT TMP_INT (synchronised by two flops) - the pin is active low. LED[0] = ALARM; LED[15:1] = 0.

"""Acceptance tests of t2_adt7420_alarm against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import cocotb
from cocotb.utils import get_sim_time
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from benchmark.lib.i2c_devices import Adt7420, I2cBus
from model import ALARM, BUSY, CTRL, DESIGN_ID, MAX, MIN, SAMPLES, STATUS, TEMP, THIGH, TLOW, Model

READING_LEN = 8                                   # log entries of one reading


# v1.2: SCL high time is 2Q to 2Q + SYNC_SLACK clocks. The spec says wait until SCL is seen high through a two-flop
# synchroniser, then 2Q: 2-3 clocks of synchroniser plus 1-3 of state and registered-output latency; 8 allows for that.
SYNC_SLACK = 8


class Env:
    def __init__(self, dut) -> None:
        self.b = Board(dut, {"dev_scl_pull": 0, "dev_sda_pull": 0, "TMP_INT": 1})
        self.dut, self.m = dut, Model()
        self.q = self.b.param("QUARTER")
        self.period = self.b.param("PERIOD_CYCLES")

    async def start(self, temp_q7: int = 0x0D87, present: bool = True) -> None:
        await self.b.start()
        self.dev = Adt7420(temp_q7, int_pin=self.dut.TMP_INT)
        self.bus = I2cBus(self.dut, [self.dev] if present else [])
        self.present = present
        self.pos = 0                               # log entries already checked
        self.done_at: list[int] = []               # clock at which each reading was seen complete

    def take(self, n: int) -> list[tuple]:
        seg = self.bus.log[self.pos:self.pos + n]
        self.pos += n
        return seg

    async def configure(self) -> None:
        await self.b.write(CTRL, 1)
        want = self.m.configure(self.present)
        await self.b.cycles(40 * 9 * (4 * self.q + 4))
        got = self.take(len(want))
        assert got == want, f"configure: bus {got} != model {want}"
        assert not self.bus.errors, self.bus.errors[:3]

    async def readings(self, n: int) -> None:
        """Wait for ``n`` more readings (each checked against the model as it ends)."""
        per = READING_LEN if self.present else 3
        for _ in range(n):
            while len(self.bus.log) < self.pos + per:
                await self.b.cycles(50)
            code = (self.dev.temp_q7 & 0xFFFF) if self.present else None
            want = self.m.reading(code)
            got = self.take(per)
            assert got == want, f"reading: bus {got} != model {want}"
            self.done_at.append(int(get_sim_time("ns")) // 10)
        assert not self.bus.errors, self.bus.errors[:3]

    async def regs(self, offs=(STATUS, TEMP, MAX, MIN, SAMPLES)) -> None:
        """Right after a reading: the registers (read before the next reading is due)."""
        for off in offs:
            got = await self.b.read(off)
            want = self.m.read(off)
            if off == STATUS:
                got &= ~BUSY
            assert got == want, f"window 0x{off:02X}: RTL 0x{got:08X}, model 0x{want:08X}"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1588660, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    assert await e.b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    for off in (CTRL, STATUS, THIGH, TLOW, TEMP, MAX, MIN, SAMPLES, 0x08, 0x7F):
        await e.b.expect(off, e.m.read(off), f"window 0x{off:02X}")
    await e.b.cycles(2 * e.period)
    assert e.bus.log == [], "I2C traffic before the configure command"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1388600, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_configure_sequence(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.b.write(THIGH, 0x0F80)                # 31 C
    e.m.write(THIGH, 0x0F80)
    await e.b.write(TLOW, 0xFF00)                 # -2 C
    e.m.write(TLOW, 0xFF00)
    await e.configure()
    assert e.dev.regs[0x03] == 0x90 and (e.dev.regs[0x04], e.dev.regs[0x05]) == (0x0F, 0x80) \
        and (e.dev.regs[0x06], e.dev.regs[0x07]) == (0xFF, 0x00), "sensor registers after configure"
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1610880, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_full_16bit_resolution(dut):
    """Trap: the textbook reads the sensor in its power-on 13-bit mode; here CONFIG bit 7 selects 16 bits, so the
    three low bits of a reading are temperature (0x0D87 = 27.05 C), not the 13-bit mode's limit flags."""
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(temp_q7=0x0D87)
    await e.configure()
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((TEMP,))
    e.dev.set_temp(-0x0123)                       # a negative reading with odd low bits
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((TEMP,))
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((TEMP, MAX, MIN))


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2639440, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_max_min_samples(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(temp_q7=0x0C00)
    await e.configure()
    for t in (0x0C00, 0x0C81, 0xFF7F, 0x0001, 0x8000, 0x7FFF, 0x0C00):
        e.dev.set_temp(t - 0x10000 if t & 0x8000 else t)
        await e.readings(1)
    gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(e.done_at, e.done_at[1:])]
    assert all(abs(g - e.period) <= 60 for g in gaps), f"readings {gaps} clocks apart, PERIOD_CYCLES {e.period}"
    await e.regs()
    await e.configure()                           # restarts the statistics
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1746300, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_alarm_follows_int(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(temp_q7=25 * 128)
    await e.b.write(THIGH, 30 * 128)
    e.m.write(THIGH, 30 * 128)
    await e.configure()
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((STATUS,))
    assert await peek(e.b.clk, dut.LED) == 0
    e.dev.set_temp(31 * 128)                      # above T_HIGH: the sensor pulls INT low
    e.m.alarm = True
    await e.b.cycles(10)
    assert int(dut.TMP_INT.value) == 0, "device model: INT should be active (low)"
    assert await peek(e.b.clk, dut.LED) == 1, "LED0 does not show the alarm"
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((STATUS,))
    e.dev.set_temp(27 * 128)                      # still above T_HIGH - T_HYST (5 C): INT stays active
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((STATUS,))
    e.dev.set_temp(24 * 128)                      # below T_HIGH - T_HYST: INT released
    e.m.alarm = False
    await e.b.cycles(10)
    assert await peek(e.b.clk, dut.LED) == 0
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((STATUS,))


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1468880, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_missing_sensor_nack(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(present=False)
    await e.configure()
    await e.readings(2)
    await e.regs()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1505880, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_clock_stretching(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.configure()
    e.bus.stretch_next = 500
    await e.readings(1)
    e.bus.stretch_next = 300
    await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs()
    hi = 2 * e.q
    assert all(hi <= h <= hi + SYNC_SLACK for h in e.bus.high), f"SCL high times {sorted(set(e.bus.high))}, 2Q = {hi}"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2004240, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_random_temperatures(dut):
    rng = random.Random(int(cocotb.RANDOM_SEED))
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start(temp_q7=rng.randrange(-40 * 128, 125 * 128))
    v = rng.randrange(1 << 16)
    await e.b.write(TLOW, v)
    e.m.write(TLOW, v)
    await e.b.expect(TLOW, e.m.read(TLOW), "TLOW")
    await e.configure()
    for _ in range(5):
        e.dev.set_temp(rng.randrange(-40 * 128, 125 * 128))
        await e.readings(1)
    await e.regs((TEMP, MAX, MIN, SAMPLES))

requirements.text: Configure writes CONFIG 0x90, T_HIGH and T_LOW in that order
Readings use a repeated START and keep the full 16-bit value
MAX, MIN, SAMPLES and VALID follow the readings; NACKs are reported and discard the reading
ALARM and LED0 follow TMP_INT, active low
On the board the reading is a plausible room temperature with odd low bits seen over time
The design closes timing at 100 MHz with no unconstrained path

resources_expected: a few hundred LUTs and FFs; no BRAM, no DSP
spec_md:
# Temperature alarm with the on-board ADT7420

Using the Nexys A7-100T's ADT7420 temperature sensor (I2C on TMP_SCL / TMP_SDA, address 0x4B), I want a
temperature monitor with a hardware alarm.

- On a configure command, set the sensor to its high-resolution 16-bit mode with the interrupt pin in comparator
  mode, active low, and load its high and low limits from two registers I write beforehand (raw sensor format).
- After that, read the temperature regularly (a parameter gives the period in clocks) and keep the raw 16-bit
  reading, the highest and lowest readings since configuring, and a count of readings.
- The alarm is the sensor's own TMP_INT pin: show it in a status bit and on LED0.
- Report I2C failures (no acknowledge) in the status.
- The usual open-drain care on the bus; the sensor may stretch the clock. SCL speed from a parameter giving a
  quarter of the SCL period in clocks (100 kHz on the board).
- Through the test shell; design ID "TALM".

Test hooks: top module `t2_adt7420_alarm_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC (`TMP_SCL`, `TMP_SDA`,
`TMP_INT`, `LED`, the USB-UART pins, `CLK100MHZ`, `CPU_RESETN`), the test shell's `CLKS_PER_BIT`,
`TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters, plus `QUARTER` (a quarter of the SCL period, in clocks) and
`PERIOD_CYCLES` (clocks between temperature readings) as top-level parameters.
title: ADT7420 16-bit temperature monitor with a comparator-mode alarm

captions: Event 0: START on the bus.
Event 1: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 2: Write 0x03: selects the CONFIG register.
Event 3: Write 0x90: data for the CONFIG register.
Event 4: STOP.
Event 5: START on the bus.
Event 6: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 7: Write 0x04: selects the T_HIGH register.
Event 8: Write 0x20: data for the T_HIGH register.
Event 9: Write 0x00: data for the T_HIGH register.
Event 10: STOP.
Event 11: START on the bus.
Event 12: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 13: Write 0x06: selects the T_LOW register.
Event 14: Write 0x05: data for the T_LOW register.
Event 15: Write 0x00: data for the T_LOW register.
Event 16: STOP.
Event 17: START on the bus.
Event 18: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 19: Write 0x00: selects the temperature register.
Event 20: Repeated START, with no STOP, so the sensor keeps its register pointer.
Event 21: Address byte 0x97 (read from 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 22: Read 0x0c, answered with ACK, one more byte to come.
Event 23: Read 0x80, answered with NACK, the last byte.
Event 24: STOP. The reading is stored: TEMP 0C80, highest 0C80, lowest 0C80, readings so far 1, alarm off.
Event 25: START on the bus.
Event 26: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 27: Write 0x00: selects the temperature register.
Event 28: Repeated START, with no STOP, so the sensor keeps its register pointer.
Event 29: Address byte 0x97 (read from 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 30: Read 0x21, answered with ACK, one more byte to come.
Event 31: Read 0x00, answered with NACK, the last byte.
Event 32: STOP. The reading is stored: TEMP 2100, highest 2100, lowest 0C80, readings so far 2, alarm on.
Event 33: START on the bus.
Event 34: Address byte 0x96 (write to 0x4b): acknowledged.
Event 35: Write 0x00: selects the temperature register.
Event 36: Repeated START, with no STOP, so the sensor keeps its register pointer.
Event 37: Address byte 0x97 (read from 0x4b): acknowledged.

Event 39: Read 0x00, answered with NACK, the last byte.
Event 40: STOP. The reading is stored: TEMP 0A00, highest 2100, lowest 0A00, readings so far 3, alarm off.
trace.stimulus: The configure command writes three register blocks (CONFIG, T_HIGH, T_LOW) to the sensor, then the model takes 3 readings that the sensor returns as 0x0c80, 0x2100, 0x0a00. The sensor's INT pin is part of the stimulus: it is held active while a reading is above T_HIGH (comparator mode), and ALARM follows it.

what: A temperature monitor that talks over I2C to the sensor chip on the board. On a configure command it sets the sensor to its high-resolution mode and loads the high and low limits the user wrote beforehand. After that it reads the temperature at regular intervals and keeps the latest, highest and lowest readings and a count. The alarm is the sensor's own interrupt pin, shown in a status bit and on an LED, and any missing acknowledgement from the sensor is reported.
where: Digital temperature sensors with a limit pin are used in computers, servers, power supplies and battery packs to raise an over-temperature alert without the processor polling. Thermal protection in an FPGA board or a data-centre server follows the same pattern.
